## Natural history notes

A microscopic freshwater green alga belonging to the desmids, characterized by very long, cylindrical cells divided into two semicells by a distinct central constriction. Triploceras verticillatum is especially distinctive because each semicell bears numerous transverse whorls of small tooth-like projections, while the ends terminate in several divergent, spine-bearing processes. It occurs in freshwater ponds, bog pools, and other standing waters, particularly in slightly acidic, nutrient-poor habitats where desmids are common. Like other desmids, it contributes to freshwater primary production and can be useful as an indicator of relatively clean, oligotrophic aquatic conditions.
